answer: Every identity carries a signal: the rhythm of its working days, kept in the Lagoon ledger for a month. A real rhythm is uneven, with sleep gaps and slow mornings; a script files at the same minute every day. The Anchor desk checks the claim against the signal within a day; a flat or borrowed rhythm means rejection and a forfeited 250-coin bond. A thousand fakes would need a thousand distinct rhythms faked day and night, plus 250,000 coins in bonds. One operator ran forty accounts from one script; all filed at the same minute each dawn, so the desk voided the whole fleet in one sweep.
